Extensions to the analysis of European COVID-19 Forecast Hub data in this repository.
The separate methods piece on evaluation design (issue #174) is sketched in `attic/evaluation-design-sketch.qmd`.
Status is taken from `submission/development-since-first-submission.md`, Appendix B.

## Temporal consistency

| Extension | Existing work | Status | Smallest next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forecast stability: how much a model revises its forecast of a fixed target week between horizons | Branch `exploratory-stability` (2bd13ae): `attic/stability.R`, `attic/stability.qmd`, Cramér distance between successive forecasts | Built, not merged | Merge the attic files to `main`; decide whether stability is a second outcome or a covariate for accuracy |
| Temporal autocorrelation in scores | `R/sensitivity/check-autocorrelation.R` | Diagnosed, not modelled; script broken since `model-logresp.R` was deleted (c5a7c93) | Point the script at the primary fit; refit with AR(1) residuals (`bam(rho = )`) and compare structure SEs |
| Lagged ensemble of the Hub ensemble | Same branch, `attic/ensemble-lag.R` | Done; negative result | None. Record the result if stability is merged |

Stability findings so far:

| Finding | Cases | Deaths |
|---|---|---|
| Revisions outside the previous forecast's 95% interval (nominal 5%) | 18% | 11% |
| Mechanistic models' coherence gap against peers on the same target, after matching | −10.7 points | −5.4 points |

Case forecasts are revised around five times as much as death forecasts.
Instability peaks with Omicron BA.1 in January 2022, the same hard period the accuracy analysis identifies, found without using observations.
Raw differences by structure mostly vanish once revisions are matched on target, as for accuracy.

## Loose ideas

From `attic/notebook.qmd`, not yet scoped:

- Simpson's paradox: cases where the ensemble moves in the opposite direction to all its components.
- Forecast trend against observed trend.
- Cramér distance among models, as model genealogy (kath-a-log #35).
- Ensemble performance as a function of size.

## Suggested order

1. Merge the stability branch: the work is done and has results.
2. Anomaly coverage check: decides whether the data-revision covariate is viable.
3. Overlap cross-tab and participation figure: descriptive, ready for the supplement if reviewers ask.
4. E-values and effective sample size.
5. US Hub port, only if a further paper needs it.
